html:
The Ikiza was the mass killing of Hutu by the Tutsi-led army and youth militia of Burundi in 1972, which killed somewhere between 100,000 and 300,000 people.

It followed a Hutu rebellion in the south at the end of April 1972, in which rebels killed thousands of Tutsi. The government of Michel Micombero answered by killing Hutu across the country, aiming above all at the educated: teachers, students, priests, clerks and soldiers. Hundreds of thousands fled to Tanzania, Rwanda and Zaire.

It left the army and state in Tutsi hands for two decades and planted fear on both sides. Many of the refugees' children joined the Hutu rebels in the civil war. In Rwanda the killings fed Hutu fears that were later used in the genocide.
sum: The Ikiza was the mass killing of Hutu by the Tutsi-led army and youth militia of Burundi in 1972, which killed somewhere between 100,000 and 300,000 people.
